items.title: Albert "June" Gardner Interview, 1996-04-17
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Earl King. The mention of 'Earl King' occurs in the [INTERVIEWER]'s turn ('...and Earl King would do this to me...'), where the interviewer describes Earl King's behavior towards the interviewer. The interviewee responds to the interviewer's anecdote but does not cla

ctx.x: Because I said, man, you want to die? No, I don't want to deal with Hampton. We were in New York. And I came home. And the next thing I knew I got a word that Wilbert was playing with him. But he played with everybody. And he was a very dear friend. But nobody mentions his name, I hope. Remember that name, New Orleans.

You know what, a lot of guys who went on the road, and Earl King would do this to me, I'll be with him and he'll say, see that guy, he's a great saxophone player. Nobody knows what, because he was always, they left. They were always gone. Yeah. So we don't, for the cats who stayed, like Red Tyler, Red didn't go on the road a lot. He was on sessions, but we know him from his records he was on.

Well that's why one of the things I used to say, if we would all leave, we wouldn't have anybody say hello to when we come back. You know what I'm saying? Everybody was leaving in the 50s and early 60s, according to California and other places. And there's a lot of people that, somebody would be talking about musicians, they'd say, well I've never heard of him. They'd say, well he's been here all his life. He played. There's quite a few guys. Harry Nance, the drummer. Been everywhere twice, played with a lot of…
